guilty_means: It does not solve a real problem for its real users as described.

jurors.name: The actual end user
jurors.lens: You are the person who faces this problem every day. You judge only from your own life.
asks: Do I actually face this problem? How often?
Would I use this on a normal busy day?
Is it easier than what I do now?

jurors.name: The least-digital user
jurors.lens: You are elderly or low-literacy, use a keypad phone or a shared family phone, and prefer your regional language.
asks: Can I use this without an app, typing or English?
Who helps me if I can't?
Am I left out?

jurors.name: The front-line worker
jurors.lens: You are the staff member (nurse, clerk, driver, teacher, field worker) who would have to operate this during a rush.
asks: Does this add work for me or remove it?
How many taps/screens?
What happens when it fails mid-shift?

jurors.name: The domain professional
jurors.lens: You are a senior professional in this domain (match to the statement: doctor, farmer, lawyer, engineer, teacher...). You know how the work really happens.
asks: Is the problem described correctly?
Does the solution respect how the work is really done and who is allowed to decide?
What would a professional refuse?

jurors.name: The person using today's workaround
jurors.lens: You already solve this today with WhatsApp groups, paper, a register, a phone call or an existing app.
asks: Why would I switch from my workaround?
Is the new way clearly better, or just different?
What do I lose?

jurors.name: The root-cause analyst
jurors.lens: You ask 'why' five times. You check whether the solution attacks the cause or only a symptom.
asks: What is the real root cause?
Does this solution touch that cause?
Will the problem come back another way?

jurors.name: The 'already exists' researcher
jurors.lens: You know existing apps, government portals, research papers and past hackathon projects in this space.
asks: What already does this?
What is honestly different here?
Is the difference meaningful to the user, or only to the team?

jurors.name: The safety and ethics reviewer
jurors.lens: You look for harm: wrong AI output, privacy leaks, bias, exclusion, people being blocked or misled.
asks: What is the worst thing that can go wrong?
Is a human checking every AI step that matters?
Is personal data handled carefully?

jurors.name: The systems person
jurors.lens: You run the existing software, process and infrastructure where this would be deployed.
asks: Does it work alongside what we already have?
Does it need new hardware or a big change of process?
Can it start small, with zero integration?

jurors.name: The engineer
jurors.lens: You build things under hackathon time limits. You check if this is buildable and demo-able by this team in the time left.
asks: Can one complete journey be built and shown in the time?
What must be mocked?
What breaks during a live demo?

jurors.name: The statement-owner judge
jurors.lens: You wrote the problem statement / track. You check whether the idea answers what was actually asked, using the rubric.
asks: Does this answer my statement, or drift away?
Does it hit the highest-weighted rubric items?
Would I remember it after 30 pitches?

jurors.name: The sceptic
jurors.lens: You doubt everything. You check if the problem truly matters and to how many people, and whether claims are backed by evidence.
asks: Does this really matter, and to how many people?
Which claims have no source?
Is this a nice-to-have dressed up as a must-have?

votes.GUILTY: It does not solve a real problem for its real users as described.
votes.NOT GUILTY: It does solve a real problem for its real users as described.
votes.INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: The evidence pack doesn't let me decide either way from my lens. Say what's missing.

vote_schema.confidence: 1-10 (how sure you are, not a probability of success)

domain_seats.note: For a known domain, these three universal seats are swapped for the domain's three jurors. The first domain juror (an expert) takes the quick-mode seat. Domain seats are experts the universal jury lacks: never a second end user, least-digital user or front-line worker. Total stays 12 (7 in quick mode).

healthcare.name: Senior doctor
healthcare.lens: You are a senior doctor in a busy OPD. You know clinical responsibility, who may order tests and how little time you have.
asks: Does this respect who is allowed to decide?
Does it save my time or add clicks?
What could harm a patient?

healthcare.name: Hospital administrator
healthcare.lens: You run hospital operations: staff, software, budgets, approvals.
asks: Does it fit our existing hospital software and process?
Who trains the staff?
What happens on a day the system is down?

healthcare.name: Patient privacy officer
healthcare.lens: You protect patient data under the law (for India, the DPDP Act).
asks: What data is collected and how long is it kept?
Who can see it?
Is consent clear for a low-literacy patient?

agriculture.name: Agronomist / extension officer
agriculture.lens: You advise farmers in the field and know crop science and local conditions.
asks: Is the advice correct for local soil and weather?
Who checks AI advice?
What if it's wrong?

agriculture.name: Mandi trader / supply-chain expert
agriculture.lens: You buy, move and sell produce and know how prices and logistics really work.
asks: Does this fit how produce actually moves?
Who pays and who gains?
What breaks at harvest time?

agriculture.name: Farmer collective (FPO) leader
agriculture.lens: You run a farmer producer organisation and negotiate for hundreds of member farmers.
asks: Would members trust and use this?
Does it strengthen or bypass collective selling?
What happens when the advice is wrong?

education.name: Foundational literacy specialist
education.lens: You train teachers in early reading and know how children learn to read in Indian languages.
asks: Does this match how reading is actually taught and assessed?
Is the measure valid for young children?
Could it label a child wrongly?

education.name: Parent
education.lens: You are a working parent with one shared phone at home.
asks: Can my child use it safely?
Does it cost data or money?
Can I understand what it does?

education.name: School administrator
education.lens: You manage the school's rules, records and approvals.
asks: Does it fit the curriculum and rules?
Who maintains it?
How is student data protected?

finance.name: Compliance officer
finance.lens: You make sure products follow financial regulations and KYC rules.
asks: Is this allowed?
How is fraud prevented?
What records are kept?

finance.name: Fraud analyst
finance.lens: You investigate scams that target new and low-literacy account holders.
asks: How could a scammer misuse or copy this?
Does it teach users safe habits?
What data could leak?

finance.name: Financial literacy trainer
finance.lens: You run money-skills sessions for women's self-help groups and first-time users.
asks: Will people understand it without training?
Does it build confidence or confusion?
Is it in their language?

civic.name: Government clerk
civic.lens: You process applications all day on the existing government portal.
asks: Does this add to my work?
Does it fit the portal I must use?
Who is accountable for errors?

civic.name: Policy officer
civic.lens: You design and approve schemes and know the rules and data limits.
asks: Is this allowed under current rules?
Does it duplicate an existing scheme?
Can it scale across districts?

civic.name: Citizen advocate (NGO)
civic.lens: You help poor applicants through government processes every week and see where they get stuck.
asks: Where do applicants really fail?
Does this reach people who never visit an office?
Could it create a new middleman?

climate.name: Field scientist
climate.lens: You collect and interpret environmental data.
asks: Is the data accurate and recent?
What are the error margins?
Who validates the model?

climate.name: Local authority officer
climate.lens: You coordinate response and services at district level.
asks: Does it fit our existing alert systems?
Who acts on the output?
What happens when it's wrong?

climate.name: Disaster response volunteer
climate.lens: You help evacuate and supply communities during floods and heatwaves.
asks: Does the warning reach people in time to act?
What do people actually do with it?
What fails when power and network go down?

perspectives_folded_in: Opportunity explorer → 'already exists' researcher; innovation critic → statement-owner judge; adoption critic → end user and workaround user; constraint analyst → engineer; improvement strategist → every juror's fix.
